titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spells 23 and 24
part: Spells 23 and 24 — opening the mouth; bringing magic (Plate 15)
about: Spells 23 and 24 follow the tribunals of Spell 18 on Plate 15 of Ani's papyrus. Spell 23 opens the dead man's mouth: Ptah, the god of his town, Thoth, Atum and Shu loosen the bonds that Seth tied on it, so that Ani can speak and breathe again, and its rubric sets all the gods against every spell spoken against him. Spell 24 brings him magic: speaking as the creator Atum-Khepri, he has it gathered from wherever it is, swifter than hounds and faster than light. Both spells are short and in places obscure, and the notes say where the reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: spell · opening · the-mouth · of · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani
sentences.i: Spell for opening the mouth of the Osiris, the scribe Ani.
sentences.n: Spell 23 begins Plate 15. The papyrus writes rꜣ wn rꜣ n in red; the name and title are black. rꜣ 'spell' is the mouth with its stroke, the noun that heads every chapter. wn 'opening' is the hare wn (E34) with water n as complement and a hatched door-leaf (coded O31, approximate) as classifier: the infinitive of wn 'open', joined to rꜣ without n, 'spell of opening'. The second rꜣ is the mouth itself, the object of the opening, and n 'of' is the genitive. wsir is written with a low seat (coded Q2, approximate) and the eye, without the seated god: Wsir N, 'the Osiris N', is the dead man named as one with Osiris. sš 'scribe' is the palette (Y3), and ꜣny has the squatting man with a flail (A52) as classifier. The opening of the mouth was the rite that gave a statue or a mummy back the use of its mouth, so that the dead could speak, eat and breathe; this spell does it for Ani himself.

sentences.i: I say: my mouth is opened by Ptah,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd·i wn rꜣ·i in in red, and Ptah's name black. ḏd·i is the cobra ḏ and the hand d, printed as one group, then the reed and a stroke. The reed is taken as the suffix ·i 'I', written here with the reed instead of the seated man, and the stroke is not read: 'I say'. Budge renders the group 'to be said', and the reading is not sure. wn is written as in the title, now with the low hooked sign (U15) under the door-leaf as a second classifier; with a noun subject and in 'by' after it, it is the passive sḏm·f, 'is opened' (it could also be a wish, 'may my mouth be opened'). rꜣ·i 'my mouth' is the mouth and its stroke with the seated man, the suffix ·i. in 'by', which names the one who does the action of a passive verb, is the reed and a curved sign (coded W25, approximate), the jar in. ptḥ 'Ptah' is p, t and the wick ḥ with the seated god (Budge: Ptaḥ). Ptah of Memphis, the craftsman among the gods, is the first of those who give Ani back his mouth.

sentences.l: are-loosened · the-bonds(?) · (twice) · which-belong-to · mouth-my · by · the-god · of-town-my
sentences.i: the bonds(?) on my mouth are loosened (Twice.) by the god of my town.
sentences.n: wḥꜥ·w is a cord sign with a hooked end on each side (coded V12, approximate), the arm ꜥ, the coil w, and the low hooked sign (U15), with a short stroke across its end, as classifier. It is taken as wḥꜥ 'loosen, untie', the cord sign standing for wḥ, and w as the ending sometimes written with the passive: 'are loosened'. Budge reads uāu, with no ḥ; the verb fits the sense, but the reading of the first sign is a guess. nwt is water n, t and the chick w: taken as a feminine plural with its ending wt written t before w, as is common, 'bonds, wrappings' (Budge: netu, 'bandages'); the word is uncertain. sp sn is the threshing floor sp (O50) with two strokes, 'twice': the words before it are to be said twice. iryw 'which belong to', here 'which are on', is the reed, r and w with a seated man wrapped in a cloak holding a stick (coded A47) and a stroke: the plural of the nisba iry, its y not written. nṯr niwt·i 'the god of my town' is the flag and the seated god, then the town sign niwt with t, a stroke and the seated man ·i; the genitive n is not written. Beside the great gods stands the god of a man's own town, the one he looked to first.

morph.gloss: bonds, wrappings (?) (noun f. plural; written n-t-w, the ending wt with t before w; sense from the context; Budge: netu, 'bandages')

sentences.l: comes · then · Thoth · filled · equipped · with · magic
sentences.i: Then Thoth comes, filled and equipped with magic,
sentences.n: ii 'come' is the sign ii (M18), a reed with legs, with the reed as complement and the walking legs (coded D54, approximate) as classifier: the sḏm·f, 'comes', or perhaps a wish, 'may Thoth come'. ir·f is the reed, r and the viper: the preposition r with the suffix ·f, written ir before a suffix, which after a verb adds weight, 'then, so'; the ·f looks forward to Thoth. ḏḥwty 'Thoth' is the ibis on its standard with t and two strokes. mḥ 'filled' is the whip mḥ (V22) with the roll, and ꜥpr 'equipped' is the bag on a cord ꜥpr (Aa20) with r and the roll: both describe Thoth, 'full and equipped'. m 'with' is the owl. ḥkꜣw 'magic' is the wick ḥ, the raised arms kꜣ (D28) with ꜣ as complement, the man with hand to mouth, the coil w and plural strokes (Budge: ḥekau). Thoth, lord of writing and of the words of power, brings the magic that frees the mouth.

sentences.l: are-loosened · the-bonds(?) · (twice) · of · Seth · which-restrain · mouth-my
sentences.i: the bonds(?) of Seth which restrain my mouth are loosened. (Twice.)
sentences.n: wḥꜥ·w and nwt are written as in line 1, and sp sn again, the strokes here under the threshing floor. n 'of' is water n. stẖ 'Seth' is the bolt s, t, a plain rectangle (coded N37, approximate) for ẖ and the seated god, as in Spell 18. sꜣw is the seated man wrapped in a cloak holding a stick (coded A47), which writes sꜣw 'guard, keep', with ꜣ and w as complements and the low hooked sign as classifier: the participle, 'which keep (shut), restrain' (Budge: sau, 'fetter'). rꜣ·i as before. Seth, the murderer of Osiris, is the power that holds the dead man's mouth shut.

morph.gloss: bonds, wrappings (?) (noun f. plural; written n-t-w, the ending wt with t before w; sense from the context; Budge: netu, 'bandages')

sentences.l: are-repelled(?) · Atum · has-cast-he · them · those-who-restrain · it
sentences.i: They are repelled(?): Atum has cast them at those who restrain it.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes wdn·n·f sn·f; read wd·n·f sn. ḫsf·tw is the spindle with a viper (coded U35), which writes ḫsf 'repel', with the low hooked sign as classifier, t and w: taken as the passive sḏm·tw·f, '(they) are repelled', the bonds of Seth being its unwritten subject (Budge: χesef-tu, 'repulsing'). It could also be read ḫsf tw tm, 'Atum repels you', with the dependent pronoun tw before the subject; the sense is not sure. tm 'Atum' is t, the sledge tm (U15) with m as complement and the seated god, the name written without its first i. It stands first, and wd·n·f takes it up: 'Atum, he has cast'. wd·n·f is the chick w and the hand d, water n, the crossed sticks (Z9) and the low hooked sign as classifiers, then n again and ·f: wdi 'put, cast' in the sḏm·n·f; the water n written before the classifiers as well as after them is a slip (Budge: uṭen-nef, 'shoots'). sn 'them' is the bolt s, water n and plural strokes, the dependent pronoun; a viper f follows it, which gives no sense and is taken as the ·f of the verb written a second time (Budge: sen-f, 'them he'). sꜣyw 'those who restrain' is the cloaked man with the stick, ꜣ, two reeds y, the chick w drawn over the low hooked sign, and a stroke: the plural participle of sꜣw. st is s and t, the dependent pronoun 'it, them', taken as the mouth. No preposition stands before sꜣyw, and 'at' is supplied from the sense. Atum, the creator, turns the bonds against the powers that tied them.

sentences.l: is-opened · mouth-my · is-parted · mouth-my · by · Shu · with · weapon(?)-his · that · of · iron · of · heaven · which · opened-he · the-mouth · of · the-gods · with-it
sentences.i: My mouth is opened, my mouth is parted by Shu with that weapon(?) of his, of the iron of heaven, with which he opened the mouth of the gods.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir; read in. After the second rꜣ·i the reed stands over an oval like the mouth r, where in 'by', the reed with water n, is meant. The papyrus writes wn rꜣ·i wp·w rꜣ·i in in red; Shu and the rest are black. wn rꜣ·i as in line 1. wp·w is the horns wp (F13) with p as complement, the crossed sticks, the chick w and the roll: wpi 'open, part', the passive with w, 'is parted' (Budge: àpu, 'be unclosed'). šw 'Shu' is the feather šw with w and the seated god. m 'with' is the sign m (Aa15). nwt·f is a weapon-like sign (coded T11, approximate; perhaps a harpoon) with t, a stroke and ·f 'his': Budge reads nut(?), 'his weapon', with a query, and the word is uncertain; it is feminine, as twy and nt show. twy 'that' is t, w and two reeds, the feminine demonstrative after its noun. nt 'of' is the feminine of the genitive. biꜣ 'iron, metal' is the foot b, the reed and ꜣ, then t over a small triangle (coded X8, approximate), a bar (coded N34, approximate) over a rectangle (coded O39, approximate), and plural strokes: the bar is the ingot, the classifier of metals, and t and the triangle are taken with the classifiers and not read (Budge: bàat). nty 'which' is water n, t and two strokes y; with im·s 'with it' at the end of the clause it makes 'with which'. wp·n·f 'he opened' is wp with p, the crossed sticks and the roll, then water n and ·f: the sḏm·n·f. rꜣ n nṯrw 'the mouth of the gods' is the mouth with its stroke, n and the flag three times. im·s is the reed and the owl, the form of m before a suffix, with the bolt ·s 'it', the feminine weapon. Shu, the air, opens the mouth for breath; biꜣ n pt, the 'iron of heaven' that falls from the sky, was the metal of the tools of the rite, here the very instrument with which the gods' own mouths were opened.

morph.gloss: a weapon or tool (?) (noun f.; written with a weapon-like sign; reading and sense uncertain; Budge: nut(?), 'weapon')

sentences.l: I · Sekhmet · sit-I · upon · the-side · of-the-West · great · of · heaven
sentences.i: I am Sekhmet; I sit on the side of the great West of heaven.
sentences.n: ink 'I' is the pot (W24), which here writes in, with the basket k and a stroke: the independent pronoun, which with a name after it makes a sentence without a verb, ink N 'I am N'. sḫmt 'Sekhmet' is a sceptre-like sign (coded S42, approximate), sḫm, with ḫ as complement, t and a seated goddess (coded B1, approximate): 'the Mighty One', the lion goddess (Budge: Seχet). ḥms·i 'I sit' is a cup with a three-pointed rim (coded N41, approximate), taken as ḥm, the bolt s, a man seated with one knee raised (coded A3, approximate) as classifier and the kneeling man ·i: the sḏm·f of ḥmsi 'sit'. ḥr 'upon' is the face with its stroke, and gs 'side' is a flat sign with a bevelled end (coded Aa13) with a stroke. imt-wrt is the reed and the owl, im with m, and t, then the swallow wr with r and t, and a hide on a forked pole (coded P5, approximate) as classifier. Budge prints it as two groups (àmt, urt), joined here as the one word it is: imy-wrt, the western side, a word first used of the starboard side of a boat, hence the classifier of sailing. Budge's numeral 5 is printed inside it, after r, and the line is kept at 4. ꜥꜣt 'great' is the column ꜥꜣ (O29) over t and the arm, with the roll, feminine to agree with imt-wrt, and nt pt 'of heaven' is the feminine genitive with p, t and the sky. The west of heaven is where the sun goes down into the world of the dead, and the fierce Sekhmet sits there on guard.

sentences.l: I · Orion · the-great · who-is-in-the-midst-of · the-bas · of-Heliopolis
sentences.i: I am Orion the great, who dwells among the bas of Heliopolis.
sentences.n: ink as before. sꜣḥ 'Orion' is a sign of toes on a base (coded D61, approximate), which writes sꜣḥ, with the star (N14) as classifier, and then a rearing serpent (coded I10, approximate) where the wick ḥ is expected, taken as ḥ (Budge: Saḥu). wr 'the great' is the swallow wr with r; Budge prints urt, but no t is written. ḥry-ib 'who is in the midst of' is the face ḥr and the heart ib, each with its stroke: the nisba of ḥr ib, 'who dwells among'. bꜣw 'the bas' is the jabiru bꜣ (G29) three times, the plural, with a stroke; the genitive n before iwnw is not written. iwnw 'Heliopolis' is the pillar iwn (O28) with the pot nw and the town sign. Sah, the constellation Orion, was the star form of Osiris in the sky, and the bas of Heliopolis are the gods of the sun's city.

morph.gloss: Sah, Orion, the constellation, the star form of Osiris (god's name; Budge: Saḥu)

sentences.l: as-for · magic · all · words · all · spoken · against-me · (swt) · stand · the-gods · against-them · the-Ennead · of-the-gods · all-together
sentences.i: As for every spell and every word spoken against me, the gods will stand up against them, the whole Ennead of the gods.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir ḥkꜣ nb ḏdt nb ḏdw r·i swt ꜥḥꜥ in red; the gods are black. ir 'as for' puts the subject first. ḥkꜣ 'magic' is written as in line 2 but without w, with a stroke, and nb 'all, every' is the basket. ḏdt 'words' is a tall tapering sign (coded U28, approximate), the fire-drill ḏꜣ, here standing for ḏ, with the hand d, t, the man with hand to mouth and a stroke. ḏdw 'spoken' is the cobra ḏ, the hand d and the chick w: the passive participle of ḏd. r·i 'against me' is r with the kneeling man ·i. swt is the sedge sw with w and t: taken as the particle swt, which stresses what comes before it; it is not translated (Budge: sut, 'these'). ꜥḥꜥ is the mast ꜥḥꜥ (P6) with the arm and the walking legs: 'stand up', the sḏm·f with nṯrw as its subject, 'the gods will stand up'. r·sn 'against them' is r, the bolt s, water n and plural strokes; n and the strokes are restored by Budge. psḏt is a round sign with markings (coded X6, the loaf) and t: taken as psḏt 'the Ennead', which Budge reads paut, the round sign standing where the sign psḏ is expected. nṯrw is the flag three times with the god and a stroke, the genitive n not written. dmḏyw is a winged sign with a crossed square (coded H5, approximate; not identified), taken as dmḏ 'unite, join', the hand d, two reeds y, w, the god and a stroke: 'united, all together' (Budge: ṭemtiu, 'all'). The Ennead, the nine gods of Heliopolis, here stands for all the gods, who defend the dead man against spells spoken against him.

sentences.l: spell · of · bringing · magic · to · the-Osiris · Ani
sentences.i: Spell for bringing magic to the Osiris Ani.
sentences.n: Spell 24 begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes rꜣ n in ḥkꜣ n in red; the name is black. in is a tall jar (coded W25, approximate), which writes in, with water n as complement: the infinitive of ini 'bring', its ending not written. ḥkꜣ 'magic' is written as in the rubric of Spell 23, and n is here the preposition 'to, for'. wsir is written as in the title of Spell 23, and ꜣny has the kneeling man with one arm raised (A1) as classifier. The magic the dead need in the world below is gathered for Ani.

sentences.l: I · Atum-Khepri · who-came-into-being · himself · upon · the-thigh · of-mother-his
sentences.i: I am Atum-Khepri, who came into being by himself upon the thigh of his mother.
sentences.n: ink as in Spell 23. tm-ḫpri is t and the sledge tm (U15, drawn with hatched cross-bars) with the seated god, then the scarab ḫpr with r, the reed and the god again: Atum and Khepri as one god, the sun at evening and at dawn, one group in Budge (Tem-χeperà). ḫpr 'who came into being' is the scarab with r, the participle. ḏs·f 'himself' is the cobra ḏ rising over the bolt s, and ·f. ḥr 'upon' is the face and r, followed by a flat sign with drooping ends (coded N1), which is not read. wꜥrt is a leg (coded D56), which writes wꜥrt, with t and the roll: 'leg, thigh' (Budge: uārt, 'the leg'). mwt·f 'his mother' is the vulture mwt with t and ·f. The creator came into being of himself, and yet is born from the lap of his mother, perhaps the sky.

sentences.l: are-given · jackals · to · those-who-are-in · Nu · hyenas · to · those-who-are-in · the-tribunal
sentences.i: Jackals are given to those who are in Nu, and hyenas to those who are in the tribunal.
sentences.n: rdi·w is the mouth r and the arm (D36), which this papyrus writes for the hand that gives, with the coil w: rdi 'give, put' in the passive with w, 'are given' (Budge: erṭāu, 'are made'). With n 'to' after the noun, 'given to' is the plain sense, but rdi … n could also mean 'made into', as Budge takes it; what the jackals and hyenas do is not said. wnšw is the hare wn with n, a rectangle with two strokes inside (coded N37, approximate) for š, w and a standing dog with a hanging tail (coded E17, approximate) with a stroke: wnš 'jackal, wolf', plural (Budge: unśu, 'wolves'). imy 'who are in' is the reed and the owl, im with m, and two strokes y; the plural w is not written, as it is in imyw after it. nw 'Nu' is the pot nw three times over the sky sign and three water lines, with the god: the primeval water. bḥnwt is the foot b, the wick ḥ, n, t and w with a dog with a curled tail (E14) and a stroke: a word for 'hyenas' (Budge: beḥennu), the t before w taken as the feminine plural ending wt; the word is not otherwise known in these parts. Budge's numeral 3 is printed inside it, after the wick, and the line is kept at 2; Budge's 'and' has no sign. imyw is im with m, two strokes, the coil w and plural strokes. ḏꜣḏꜣt 'the tribunal' is spelled as in Spell 18, the fire-drill twice with a small ring, t, a barred sign and the god (Budge: t'at'at, 'the divine chiefs'). Jackals and hyenas are the scavengers of the desert edge where the dead are buried.

sentences.l: now · have-gathered-(I) · magic · this · which-it(-is) · with · the-man · which-it(-is) · with-him · swifter · than · hounds · faster · than · light
sentences.i: Now I have gathered this magic, which is with the man with whom it is, swifter than hounds, faster than light.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ist dmḏ·n·(i) ḥkꜣw pn nty·f ḫr s nty·f ḫr·f btnw in red, and the rest black. ist 'now' is the reed, s and t, the particle that opens a statement. dmḏ·n·(i) is the winged sign coded H5 (approximate), taken as dmḏ 'gather, join' as in Spell 23, with d, the roll and water n: the sḏm·n·f, 'I have gathered', its subject ·i not written, as often (Budge: ṭemṭ-nà, 'I collect'). ḥkꜣw has the coil w here; pn 'this' is p and n. nty·f is water n and t with ·f: the relative nty with a suffix, 'which it (is)', its y not written. The second and third versions below have m bw nb nty·f im 'from every place where it is'; here m bw nb and im are left out, and what stands is translated. ḫr 'with' (of persons) is ḫ and r; s 'man' is the bolt s with a stroke and the kneeling man; ḫr·f 'with him' is ḫ, r and ·f. btnw is t (printed before the foot), the foot b, n over the pot nw, w and the walking legs: btn 'be swift', with r 'than' after it, the comparison (Budge: betennu, 'quicker'). ṯsm 'hound' is the tethering rope ṯ, the bolt s, the sign m and a dog with a curled tail (E14), the hunting dog (Budge: θesem). ḫꜣḫ 'fast' is a tall stem with a curled top (coded M12, approximate), ḫꜣ, with ꜣ, ḫ, the walking legs and a stroke. The r 'than' that follows is restored by Budge. šwyt is the feather šw with w, two reeds y, t and the sun: taken with Budge as 'light', perhaps a word from šw 'sunlight'; the reading is uncertain. The magic comes faster than anything that runs or shines.

sentences.l: O · who-brings · the-ferry-boat · of · Ra · are-firm · ropes(?)-your · in · the-north-wind · as · sailing-upstream-your · to · the-Lake-of-Fire · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: O you who bring the ferry-boat of Ra, your ropes(?) are firm in the north wind as you sail upstream to the Lake of Fire in the necropolis.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i inn mꜥẖnt nt in red; Ra and the rest are black. i 'O' is the reed with the man with hand to mouth. inn 'who brings' is the jar in (coded W25, approximate) with water n twice: the participle of ini, its n doubled (Budge: ànen, 'bringer'). mꜥẖnt 'ferry-boat' is the owl m drawn across the arm ꜥ, the belly of an animal ẖ (coded F32, approximate), n, t and a boat (coded P1, approximate): mḫnt 'ferry-boat', written here with ꜥ and ẖ (Budge: māχent). nt is the feminine of the genitive. rꜥ 'Ra' is the seated god with the sun on his head (C1). rwd 'firm' is r, the hand d and w before a loop with a crossing stick (coded T12, approximate), which writes rwd, and the roll: the stative, 'are firm'. ꜥqy·k is the arm ꜥ, the hill-slope q (N29), two strokes y, two sticks bent over at the top (coded S39, approximate; not identified) as classifiers, and ·k 'your': a word for some part of a boat's tackle, taken as 'ropes' with a query (Budge: āqi-k, 'thy sail and rudder ropes'). mḥyt 'the north wind' is the whip mḥ (V22) with ḥ, two reeds, a hide on a forked pole (coded P5, approximate; the sail, classifier of wind) and t. m ḫnt·k 'as you sail upstream' is the owl m and a rack of jars ḫnt (W17) with n and t, the sail and a boat as classifiers, and ·k: the infinitive of ḫnti 'sail upstream' with a suffix as its subject. š-nsrt 'the Lake of Fire' is a pool (N37) over a small triangle (coded X8, approximate) and a stroke, then two flame signs (coded Q7, approximate), which write nsrt 'flame', and a small round sign (coded O49, approximate) (Budge: Śe-nesert). m 'in' is written twice, the owl and the sign m (Aa15), and read once. ẖrt-nṯr is the flag nṯr, written first out of respect, with r and the butcher's block ẖr (T28) in one group, its t not written: 'the necropolis' (Budge: neter-χert). The north wind fills the sail of a boat going south, upstream; the Lake of Fire is a lake of the world below.

sentences.l: now · have-gathered-you · magic · this · from · place · every · which-it(-is) · there · from · the-man · which-it(-is) · with-him · swifter · than · hounds · faster · than · light
sentences.i: Now you have gathered this magic from every place where it is, from the man with whom it is, swifter than hounds, faster than light.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes isk dmḏ·n·k ḥkꜣw pn in red; the rest is black. isk is the reed, s and the basket k: the particle isk 'now, see', another form of ist. dmḏ·n·k is written as in line 3, with ·k 'you' as its subject (Budge: 'thou collectest'): here it is the one addressed who has gathered the magic, where the first and third versions say 'I'. Budge's numeral 5 is printed inside ḥkꜣw, before the man with hand to mouth, and the line is kept at 4. m bw nb 'from every place' is the owl, bw (the foot b and w) and the basket. nty·f im 'where it is' is nty (n, t and two strokes y) with ·f, and im 'there', the reed and the owl: 'which it (is) there', the Egyptian way of saying 'where'. The viper ·f is restored by Budge, here and in the nty·f that follows; Budge prints nty and ·f as two groups, and they are joined here. ḫr s nty·f ḫr·f 'from the man with whom it is' as in line 3. btnw is here b, t, n, w, the walking legs and plural strokes, ṯsmw has the coil w of the plural, ḫꜣḫt is written with t, and šwyt without the chick w. The same refrain closes each of the three versions.

sentences.l: making · forms · from · the-thigh(?) · of-the-mother · as · are-created · the-gods · from · silence · was-given · the-mother(?) · heat · to · the-gods
sentences.i: making forms from the thigh(?) of the mother, as the gods are created from silence; the mother(?) was given heat for the gods.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes irt ḫprw m in red. irt is the eye ir with t: taken as the infinitive of iri 'make', 'making', which goes on from the magic before it; ḫprw 'forms' is the scarab with r and w, the standing mummy (A53) and a stroke, and irt ḫprw is 'to take on forms'. rtw is r, t and w: Budge renders 'the thigh' with a query, and it is taken as a writing of rd 'leg', with t for d; the reading is uncertain. mwt 'the mother' is t, printed before the vulture, and the vulture mwt. The owl m after it has no English in Budge, and is taken as 'as, while' before the clause that follows. qmꜣ·tw is the hill-slope q, a vulture with a throw-stick drawn across its back (the vulture ꜣ and the throw-stick, coded T14, approximate), the owl m, a tall plant-like sign (coded M15, approximate) and the roll as classifiers, then t and w: qmꜣ 'create' with ·tw, the passive, 'are created' (Budge: qemam-tu, 'creating'). The owl m 'from' before sgrw is restored by Budge. sgrw is the folded cloth s, the jar-stand g (W11), r and w with the man with hand to mouth and a stroke: 'silence', from sgr 'make quiet' (Budge: seḳeru). rdi·n·tw is r, the arm, water n, t and w: rdi in the passive sḏm·n·tw·f, 'was given'. mwt is the vulture alone; Budge marks 'the mother' with a query, and so does the rendering. srf 'heat, warmth' is the bolt s, r and f with a flame (coded Q7, approximate) as classifier; n nṯrw 'to, for the gods'. How these words hang together is not clear, and the rendering follows the order of the signs. They speak of the magic of creation: taking forms, the gods coming out of silence, the warmth that gives life.

morph.gloss: silence, stillness (noun; from sgr 'make quiet'; Budge: seḳeru)

sentences.l: now · is-given · to-me · magic · this · from · him-whose(-is)-it · swifter · than · hounds · faster · than · light
sentences.i: Now this magic is given to me from the one who has it, swifter than hounds, faster than light.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes istw … n·i in red. rdi, between them, is restored by Budge, the mouth r and the arm with a loaf (D37), and his overline covers only n·i. istw is ist with the chick w. Budge prints rdi and n·i as one group (erṭā-nà, 'is given to me'); it is split here into rdi, the passive sḏm·f, 'is given', and n·i 'to me', water n and the kneeling man, the preposition with its suffix, which Egyptian puts before a noun subject. ḥkꜣ is written with a small caret (coded D54, approximate) where the coil w stands in the other writings, and the caret is not read. ipn is the reed, p and n, the plural demonstrative 'these', agreeing with ḥkꜣ as 'spells'; it is rendered with the collective 'this magic'. ḫr nty·f is ḫr 'from, with' (of persons) and nty·f, here n, t, two strokes and ·f: nty as a noun, 'him whose it is', the one who has it (Budge: 'where it is'); the sense is uncertain. Budge's line 7 begins with btnw, written with the pot nw as in line 3; in ṯsmw the tethering rope ṯ is restored by Budge, and m is the owl. In this third version the speaker again says 'I'.

sentences.i: Another saying: faster than a shadow(?).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. ky 'other' is the basket k with two reeds y, and ḏd 'saying' is the cobra and the hand: ky ḏd 'another saying', which brings in a variant of the words before. ḫꜣḫ r as before. šwt is written like šwyt in the refrain, the feather, w, two reeds and t, but with an open rectangle (coded O1) as classifier in place of the sun; Budge renders 'a shadow' with a query, and it is taken as šwt 'shade, shadow', a different word from the 'light' of the refrain; the reading is uncertain. Spell 24 ends here. Other papyri go on with Spell 25, a spell for making a man remember his name in the world below, which Budge prints next from the papyrus of Nebseni; Ani's papyrus does not have it.

morph.gloss: shade, shadow (noun f.; here written šwyt, with a house-like classifier; reading uncertain; Budge: śuit, 'a shadow (?)')
